name: Tailender Tom Brain
description: Expanded offline Q&A, training cards, troubleshooting flows, glossary, and Easy English helper content for Christian field recording teams.

items.question: How do I find new languages in a region?
items.answer: Start by checking the MAP app to see existing data for your current location. Talk to local market traders, religious leaders, and transporters who travel between villages. Always verify 'web' or 'map' data with real people in the field.
items.easyEnglish: Check the MAP app first. Then talk to local people who travel. Always check the information yourself.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; finding and verifying new speech communities

items.question: How do I know this is the right heart language?
items.answer: Check what people use at home, with family, in worship, and when telling stories. Compare outside data with local interviews. A trade language may be useful, but the heart language is usually the language that carries deep meaning and trust.
items.easyEnglish: Check what people use at home, with family, in worship, and when telling stories. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What is the difference between a trade language and a mother tongue?
items.answer: A trade language is used for business, government, school, or communication with outsiders. A mother tongue is the language learned at home and often used for family, feelings, stories, and faith questions.
items.easyEnglish: A trade language is used for business, government, school, or communication with outsiders. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What if two villages say they speak the same language but sound different?
items.answer: Treat this as a dialect question. Record short samples or word lists from both places, ask trusted listeners about understanding and acceptability, and write the difference in the Language & Community Profile.
items.easyEnglish: Treat this as a dialect question. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What natural boundaries can affect dialects?
items.answer: Rivers, mountains, roads, migration patterns, marriage patterns, schools, markets, and religious networks can separate or connect speech communities. Do not assume nearby villages understand each other the same way.
items.easyEnglish: Rivers, mountains, roads, migration patterns, marriage patterns, schools, markets, and religious networks can separate or connect speech communities. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: Can I copy language data from a website?
items.answer: Use websites as a starting point, not the final answer. Copying without field verification can send a team to the wrong people or wrong dialect. Mark web-only information as likely or unknown until confirmed locally.
items.easyEnglish: Use websites as a starting point, not the final answer. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What should I do if websites disagree about a language?
items.answer: Write down the disagreement, record the source names, and verify through local interviews or partner knowledge. Do not hide uncertainty; make it visible so the team can solve it.
items.easyEnglish: Write down the disagreement, record the source names, and verify through local interviews or partner knowledge. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: How do I know if recordings already exist?
items.answer: Search the organization’s records, partner libraries, Scripture resources, and local churches. Ask whether the recordings are understandable, available, current, and actually being used.
items.easyEnglish: Search the organization’s records, partner libraries, Scripture resources, and local churches. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What if an old recording exists but people do not use it?
items.answer: Find out why. It may be the wrong dialect, poor audio, old vocabulary, hard access, weak distribution, or lack of local ownership. A new project may still be needed, but the reason should be clear.
items.easyEnglish: Find out why. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: Who can verify language information?
items.answer: Use a mix of local believers, community leaders, language helpers, teachers, translators, field workers, and ordinary listeners. One person’s opinion is helpful but not always enough.
items.easyEnglish: Use a mix of local believers, community leaders, language helpers, teachers, translators, field workers, and ordinary listeners. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What is a cultural bridge?
items.answer: A cultural bridge is a local story, proverb, object, practice, or experience that helps people understand a message. It should clarify the message without changing biblical truth.
items.easyEnglish: A cultural bridge is a local story, proverb, object, practice, or experience that helps people understand a message. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What cultural notes should I treat carefully?
items.answer: Treat conflict, shame, family roles, religious identity, political pressure, persecution risk, gender norms, and public naming carefully. Write facts respectfully and avoid gossip.
items.easyEnglish: Treat conflict, shame, family roles, religious identity, political pressure, persecution risk, gender norms, and public naming carefully. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: What should be complete before Research is done?
items.answer: You should have a language/community profile, local verification notes, dialect confidence, target listener notes, existing resource check, cultural bridge notes, and open questions marked clearly.
items.easyEnglish: You should have a language/community profile, local verification notes, dialect confidence, target listener notes, existing resource check, cultural bridge notes, and open questions marked clearly. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Research phase; heart-language and local verification principles

items.question: How do I choose a script?
items.answer: Choose a script that fits the audience, purpose, language ability, time limit, and ministry setting. A children’s lesson, testimony, Gospel story, worship song, or health/help message should not all be planned the same way.
items.easyEnglish: Choose a script that fits the audience, purpose, language ability, time limit, and ministry setting. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: Should we translate word-for-word?
items.answer: Usually no. Keep the meaning and biblical truth, but use natural wording in the target language. Ask a local helper how their grandmother or respected elder would say it.
items.easyEnglish: Usually no. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What is back-translation?
items.answer: Back-translation is when someone translates the target-language draft back into a language reviewers understand. It helps catch missing meaning, added ideas, and confusing terms.
items.easyEnglish: Back-translation is when someone translates the target-language draft back into a language reviewers understand. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What words may need special care?
items.answer: Words like sin, grace, repent, sacrifice, kingdom, spirit, demon, eternal life, forgive, born again, holy, and Savior may need careful local explanation.
items.easyEnglish: Words like sin, grace, repent, sacrifice, kingdom, spirit, demon, eternal life, forgive, born again, holy, and Savior may need careful local explanation. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: How do we protect biblical accuracy?
items.answer: Use Scripture references, theological review, back-translation, local believer review, and careful notes on changed wording. Natural language does not mean loose doctrine.
items.easyEnglish: Use Scripture references, theological review, back-translation, local believer review, and careful notes on changed wording. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: Can we replace Bible animals or objects with local ones?
items.answer: Be careful. A local bridge can help explain, but do not change a biblical detail in a way that changes meaning. If the script mentions a lamb and listeners know goats better, add a clarifying bridge instead of casually rewriting Scripture.
items.easyEnglish: Be careful. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: When do we need permission?
items.answer: Get permission when using someone else’s script, song, music, photo, video, translation, testimony, name, or voice in ways beyond private practice.
items.easyEnglish: Get permission when using someone else’s script, song, music, photo, video, translation, testimony, name, or voice in ways beyond private practice. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What should a speaker understand before giving consent?
items.answer: They should understand what will be recorded, who may hear it, whether it can be shared online or offline, whether their name/photo will be used, and whether there are restrictions.
items.easyEnglish: They should understand what will be recorded, who may hear it, whether it can be shared online or offline, whether their name/photo will be used, and whether there are restrictions. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What makes a good speaker?
items.answer: A good speaker is understandable, locally accepted, patient, willing, and natural. Reading ability helps, but a trusted natural storyteller may be better than a stiff reader.
items.easyEnglish: A good speaker is understandable, locally accepted, patient, willing, and natural. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What can a language helper do?
items.answer: A helper can translate, explain culture, coach pronunciation, check meaning, recruit speakers, note mistakes, and help the team avoid shame or confusion.
items.easyEnglish: A helper can translate, explain culture, coach pronunciation, check meaning, recruit speakers, note mistakes, and help the team avoid shame or confusion. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What should be planned before recording day?
items.answer: Plan location, time, speakers, helpers, transport, food/water, equipment, power, forms, backup, permissions, quiet space, and a realistic session schedule.
items.easyEnglish: Plan location, time, speakers, helpers, transport, food/water, equipment, power, forms, backup, permissions, quiet space, and a realistic session schedule. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What risks should the team write down?
items.answer: Write down safety concerns, local conflict, weather, travel, power, illness, permission delays, sensitive topics, and risk to believers or speakers.
items.easyEnglish: Write down safety concerns, local conflict, weather, travel, power, illness, permission delays, sensitive topics, and risk to believers or speakers. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: Why plan Share before Record?
items.answer: The final use affects length, format, language, file names, permissions, and follow-up. A recording for radio, WhatsApp, SD card, or listening group may need different decisions.
items.easyEnglish: The final use affects length, format, language, file names, permissions, and follow-up. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What should be complete before Plan is done?
items.answer: You need a clear purpose, approved content path, speaker/helper plan, permissions plan, theological/local review plan, recording location, equipment checklist, backup plan, and sharing path.
items.easyEnglish: You need a clear purpose, approved content path, speaker/helper plan, permissions plan, theological/local review plan, recording location, equipment checklist, backup plan, and sharing path. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Planning and scripting guidance; permissions and adaptation

items.question: What is the first thing to do before pressing Record?
items.answer: Make a short test recording and listen with headphones. Check microphone, level, noise, speaker comfort, and room tone before the real take.
items.easyEnglish: Make a short test recording and listen with headphones. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: How long should room tone be?
items.answer: Capture about 20 to 30 seconds of quiet room tone in the same place, with the same microphone position, before or during the session.
items.easyEnglish: Capture about 20 to 30 seconds of quiet room tone in the same place, with the same microphone position, before or during the session. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: How loud should the recording be?
items.answer: Record strong but safe. Avoid red peaks or distortion. It is better to have clean audio that is a little low than loud audio that is clipped.
items.easyEnglish: Record strong but safe. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: What should I do if the audio clips?
items.answer: Stop, lower the input gain or move the microphone slightly away, and retake the section. Clipped audio cannot be fully repaired later.
items.easyEnglish: Stop, lower the input gain or move the microphone slightly away, and retake the section. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: What noise should I watch for?
items.answer: Fans, fridges, generators, wind, rain, traffic, animals, phones, bracelets, chairs, papers, echo, and people outside can all hurt a recording.
items.easyEnglish: Fans, fridges, generators, wind, rain, traffic, animals, phones, bracelets, chairs, papers, echo, and people outside can all hurt a recording. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: Where should I place the microphone?
items.answer: Place it close enough for clear voice but not directly in the blast of breath. Slightly off to the side often reduces pops while keeping the voice clear.
items.easyEnglish: Place it close enough for clear voice but not directly in the blast of breath. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: How do I help a nervous speaker?
items.answer: Explain the process simply, record a practice line, encourage normal speech, allow breaks, and keep correction gentle. Protect the speaker’s dignity.
items.easyEnglish: Explain the process simply, record a practice line, encourage normal speech, allow breaks, and keep correction gentle. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: What if the speaker makes a mistake?
items.answer: Pause calmly, mark the mistake, and restart from a natural sentence break. Do not talk over the mistake if the recorder is still running unless that is your team method.
items.easyEnglish: Pause calmly, mark the mistake, and restart from a natural sentence break. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: How do I mark the best take?
items.answer: Write the file name, take number, script section, and why it is best. If possible, mark the best take before leaving the session.
items.easyEnglish: Write the file name, take number, script section, and why it is best. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: Do we need to listen back before leaving?
items.answer: Yes. Listen to a sample or full take if possible. Check that the file exists, audio is clear, no severe clipping occurred, and the correct speaker/script was recorded.
items.easyEnglish: Yes. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: How many backups do we need?
items.answer: At least one backup before leaving; two is better. Keep copies on separate devices when possible.
items.easyEnglish: At least one backup before leaving; two is better. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: What should be complete before Record is done?
items.answer: Session log, speaker consent, room tone, test recording, usable takes, best take notes, noise/retake notes, playback check, and backup status should be complete.
items.easyEnglish: Session log, speaker consent, room tone, test recording, usable takes, best take notes, noise/retake notes, playback check, and backup status should be complete. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Recording phase; standards, documentation, room tone, backup

items.question: What is Program stage for?
items.answer: Program turns raw or edited recordings into a usable final product with clear order, titles, metadata, file names, and purpose.
items.easyEnglish: Program turns raw or edited recordings into a usable final product with clear order, titles, metadata, file names, and purpose. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: What belongs in a tracklist?
items.answer: Track number, title, speaker/singer, script or song name, duration, Scripture references, notes, and final file name.
items.easyEnglish: Track number, title, speaker/singer, script or song name, duration, Scripture references, notes, and final file name. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: How do I decide track order?
items.answer: Choose an order that helps listeners understand and respond. Keep stories, teaching, songs, and calls to action in a clear sequence.
items.easyEnglish: Choose an order that helps listeners understand and respond. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: Why does file naming matter?
items.answer: Clear file names prevent lost audio, slow review, and wrong uploads. Names should help another worker understand the file without asking you.
items.easyEnglish: Clear file names prevent lost audio, slow review, and wrong uploads. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: Should I rename original recorder files?
items.answer: Usually keep originals safe and create clean copies with better names. Do not destroy or overwrite original field recordings.
items.easyEnglish: Usually keep originals safe and create clean copies with better names. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: What metadata should be checked?
items.answer: Language, dialect, project, speaker, title, Scripture, content type, duration, permissions, track order, and version status.
items.easyEnglish: Language, dialect, project, speaker, title, Scripture, content type, duration, permissions, track order, and version status. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: What quality checks belong in Program?
items.answer: Check clean audio, correct edits, no missing tracks, no wrong language labels, no missing permissions, and no mismatch between script and audio.
items.easyEnglish: Check clean audio, correct edits, no missing tracks, no wrong language labels, no missing permissions, and no mismatch between script and audio. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: What if the program includes songs?
items.answer: Record song title, singer/group, owner if known, permission, language, meaning, and allowed sharing methods.
items.easyEnglish: Record song title, singer/group, owner if known, permission, language, meaning, and allowed sharing methods. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: How do I handle versions?
items.answer: Use simple labels such as draft, reviewed, final, corrected, or published. Avoid sending a draft file as final by mistake.
items.easyEnglish: Use simple labels such as draft, reviewed, final, corrected, or published. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: What should be complete before Program is done?
items.answer: Track order, program title, file names, metadata, duration, speaker/script info, permissions check, quality check, and package preview should be complete.
items.easyEnglish: Track order, program title, file names, metadata, duration, speaker/script info, permissions check, quality check, and package preview should be complete. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Program phase; naming, metadata, final product organization

items.question: What is Submit?
items.answer: Submit is the handoff of a complete recording package to the reviewer, media team, studio, database team, ministry office, or publishing process.
items.easyEnglish: Submit is the handoff of a complete recording package to the reviewer, media team, studio, database team, ministry office, or publishing process. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: What goes in a submission package?
items.answer: Final audio, original or edited files if required, scripts, translations/back-translations, forms, permissions, tracklist, metadata, notes, and reviewer questions.
items.easyEnglish: Final audio, original or edited files if required, scripts, translations/back-translations, forms, permissions, tracklist, metadata, notes, and reviewer questions. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: Why send a complete package the first time?
items.answer: Incomplete packages create delays, repeated questions, lost files, and stress for reviewers and field teams. A complete package speeds ministry use.
items.easyEnglish: Incomplete packages create delays, repeated questions, lost files, and stress for reviewers and field teams. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: What status should I choose?
items.answer: Use simple status labels: Draft, Ready to Submit, Submitted, Needs Correction, Approved, Published, or Archived.
items.easyEnglish: Use simple status labels: Draft, Ready to Submit, Submitted, Needs Correction, Approved, Published, or Archived. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: What should I ask the reviewer?
items.answer: Ask about theological clarity, cultural concerns, technical issues, missing metadata, permissions, and whether anything blocks sharing.
items.easyEnglish: Ask about theological clarity, cultural concerns, technical issues, missing metadata, permissions, and whether anything blocks sharing. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: What if the reviewer requests changes?
items.answer: Do not overwrite the original package. Make a corrected version, write what changed, update the status, and keep the old version if needed.
items.easyEnglish: Do not overwrite the original package. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: What if internet is too weak to upload?
items.answer: Prepare a physical or delayed transfer plan: USB, SD card, external drive, local partner upload, or compressed package if allowed. Keep the package organized.
items.easyEnglish: Prepare a physical or delayed transfer plan: USB, SD card, external drive, local partner upload, or compressed package if allowed. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: Should I back up before submitting?
items.answer: Yes. Back up the full package before sending. Submission is not a replacement for your own safe copy.
items.easyEnglish: Yes. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: What should be complete before Submit is done?
items.answer: Package checklist, forms, permissions, tracklist, metadata, backup, submitted-to person/place, date, status, and reviewer notes should be complete.
items.easyEnglish: Package checklist, forms, permissions, tracklist, metadata, backup, submitted-to person/place, date, status, and reviewer notes should be complete. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: Why does Share come after Submit?
items.answer: Submit is the handoff; Share is the ministry distribution and follow-up. A recording can be submitted but still not reach listeners yet.
items.easyEnglish: Submit is the handoff; Share is the ministry distribution and follow-up. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submit phase; complete package, status, distribution thinking

items.question: What is Share?
items.answer: Share means the finished message reaches real listeners through churches, believers, field workers, phones, SD cards, Bluetooth, QR codes, radio, speaker boxes, or listening groups.
items.easyEnglish: Share means the finished message reaches real listeners through churches, believers, field workers, phones, SD cards, Bluetooth, QR codes, radio, speaker boxes, or listening groups. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: How can we share without internet?
items.answer: Use SD cards, USB drives, Bluetooth, phone-to-phone sharing, speaker boxes, local Wi-Fi sharing, printed instructions, and listening groups.
items.easyEnglish: Use SD cards, USB drives, Bluetooth, phone-to-phone sharing, speaker boxes, local Wi-Fi sharing, printed instructions, and listening groups. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: How can we share online wisely?
items.answer: Use approved links, ministry pages, apps, or messaging platforms. Confirm permissions, safety, and whether public sharing could put speakers or believers at risk.
items.easyEnglish: Use approved links, ministry pages, apps, or messaging platforms. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: What should a QR code point to?
items.answer: Point it to a stable, tested page or file location where the correct language content is easy to access. Test it on a phone before printing.
items.easyEnglish: Point it to a stable, tested page or file location where the correct language content is easy to access. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: How can local churches use the recordings?
items.answer: They can use them for evangelism, discipleship, children’s ministry, women’s ministry, listening groups, visitation, follow-up, and church planting support.
items.easyEnglish: They can use them for evangelism, discipleship, children’s ministry, women’s ministry, listening groups, visitation, follow-up, and church planting support. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: How do we plan a listening group?
items.answer: Plan who invites people, where they meet, what track is played, who leads discussion, how questions are handled, and how follow-up happens.
items.easyEnglish: Plan who invites people, where they meet, what track is played, who leads discussion, how questions are handled, and how follow-up happens. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: What feedback should we collect?
items.answer: Collect whether the language was understandable, the message was clear, people listened, questions came up, objections appeared, and what content is needed next.
items.easyEnglish: Collect whether the language was understandable, the message was clear, people listened, questions came up, objections appeared, and what content is needed next. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: When should we avoid public sharing?
items.answer: Avoid public sharing when it may endanger speakers, believers, churches, or communities, or when permission is limited to local/private use.
items.easyEnglish: Avoid public sharing when it may endanger speakers, believers, churches, or communities, or when permission is limited to local/private use. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: How do we know Share worked?
items.answer: Look for access, understanding, use by local partners, listener response, questions, testimonies, requests for more content, and clear next steps.
items.easyEnglish: Look for access, understanding, use by local partners, listener response, questions, testimonies, requests for more content, and clear next steps. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: What should be complete before Share is done?
items.answer: Sharing method, local partner, permission check, target listeners, follow-up contact, feedback plan, and response notes should be complete.
items.easyEnglish: Sharing method, local partner, permission check, target listeners, follow-up contact, feedback plan, and response notes should be complete. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Submission & distribution guidance; Share added for Christian workflow

items.question: What is the Language & Community Profile for?
items.answer: It stores the research facts about language, dialect, people, location, existing resources, contacts, and confidence level.
items.easyEnglish: It stores the research facts about language, dialect, people, location, existing resources, contacts, and confidence level. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Neutral form pack placement

items.question: What is the Recording Project Plan for?
items.answer: It keeps purpose, audience, content, Scripture, logistics, equipment, permissions, backup, and sharing plan in one place.
items.easyEnglish: It keeps purpose, audience, content, Scripture, logistics, equipment, permissions, backup, and sharing plan in one place. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Neutral form pack placement

items.question: What is the Speaker & Helper Consent Form for?
items.answer: It records whether a person agrees to be recorded and how their voice, name, photo, or contribution may be used.
items.easyEnglish: It records whether a person agrees to be recorded and how their voice, name, photo, or contribution may be used. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Neutral form pack placement

items.question: What is the Script & Content Approval Form for?
items.answer: It tracks script source, translation/adaptation, back-translation, theological review, local review, sensitive terms, and approval status.
items.easyEnglish: It tracks script source, translation/adaptation, back-translation, theological review, local review, sensitive terms, and approval status. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.

items.question: What is the Recording Session Log for?
items.answer: It records what happened in a session: file names, takes, best take, equipment, room tone, noise, playback, and backup.
items.easyEnglish: It records what happened in a session: file names, takes, best take, equipment, room tone, noise, playback, and backup. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.

items.question: What is the Audio Program Form for?
items.answer: It describes the final program: title, track order, speakers, durations, Scripture, music, notes, and final file names.

items.question: What is the Sharing & Distribution Plan for?
items.answer: It helps the team move from finished recording to real listener access through local and digital channels.
items.easyEnglish: It helps the team move from finished recording to real listener access through local and digital channels. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.

items.question: What is the Field Feedback Form for?
items.answer: It captures response after sharing: understanding, objections, testimonies, questions, requests, corrections, and follow-up.
items.easyEnglish: It captures response after sharing: understanding, objections, testimonies, questions, requests, corrections, and follow-up. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.

items.question: The recording sounds distorted. What do I do?
items.answer: Distortion often means clipping or microphone overload. Lower the input gain, move the mic slightly away, retake the section, and mark the bad take so it is not used.
items.easyEnglish: Distortion often means clipping or microphone overload. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: The recording is too quiet. What do I do?
items.answer: Check the microphone connection, move closer, raise gain carefully, and record a new test. Do not depend on editing to fix a very weak recording.
items.easyEnglish: Check the microphone connection, move closer, raise gain carefully, and record a new test. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: There is wind noise. What do I do?
items.answer: Move indoors or behind a wind block, use a windscreen, turn the microphone away from direct wind, and retest before continuing.
items.easyEnglish: Move indoors or behind a wind block, use a windscreen, turn the microphone away from direct wind, and retest before continuing. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: There is hum or buzz. What do I do?
items.answer: Check lights, chargers, power cables, generators, laptops, and nearby electronics. Try battery power and move audio cables away from power cables.
items.easyEnglish: Check lights, chargers, power cables, generators, laptops, and nearby electronics. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: The room is echoey. What do I do?
items.answer: Move to a smaller or softer space, add blankets or curtains, avoid bare walls, and keep the mic closer to the speaker.
items.easyEnglish: Move to a smaller or softer space, add blankets or curtains, avoid bare walls, and keep the mic closer to the speaker. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: The speaker pops P and B sounds. What do I do?
items.answer: Move the microphone slightly off-axis, add a pop filter or windscreen, and ask for natural speech instead of strong projection.
items.easyEnglish: Move the microphone slightly off-axis, add a pop filter or windscreen, and ask for natural speech instead of strong projection. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: Tailender Tom gives the wrong answer. What do I do?
items.answer: Try a shorter question with key words like room tone, consent, submit, or heart language. If still wrong, save the question for review and add a better Q&A later.
items.easyEnglish: Try a shorter question with key words like room tone, consent, submit, or heart language. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: Tailender Tom says he does not know. What now?
items.answer: That means the offline database has no good match yet. Save the question, ask a trainer or reviewer, then add the approved answer to the database.
items.easyEnglish: That means the offline database has no good match yet. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: The app is blank. What should I check?
items.answer: Restart the dev server, check browser console errors, confirm index.html points to /src/main.tsx, and confirm the latest code was saved.
items.easyEnglish: Restart the dev server, check browser console errors, confirm index. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: The logo is missing. What should I check?
items.answer: Confirm the image is in public/icons/tailender-buckle.png and the app uses /icons/tailender-buckle.png, not a src folder path.
items.easyEnglish: Confirm the image is in public/icons/tailender-buckle. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: The PWA will not install. What should I check?
items.answer: Check manifest, service worker registration, icon paths, localhost/HTTPS, and console errors. Restart the app after changing manifest or service worker.
items.easyEnglish: Check manifest, service worker registration, icon paths, localhost/HTTPS, and console errors. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: GitHub Desktop wants to commit a backup folder. What should I do?
items.answer: Move the backup outside the repo, delete it after testing, or add it to .gitignore. Do not commit temporary backup folders.
items.easyEnglish: Move the backup outside the repo, delete it after testing, or add it to. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: I cannot find a recording. What do I search?
items.answer: Search project name, date, language, speaker, recorder file name, track number, and backup drive. Check originals, edited files, program exports, memory card, and ZIP package.
items.easyEnglish: Search project name, date, language, speaker, recorder file name, track number, and backup drive. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: Device storage is full. What do I do?
items.answer: Stop importing new files. Back up originals, remove duplicate exports and temporary files, empty trash if safe, and keep the final package organized.
items.easyEnglish: Stop importing new files. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: We have no internet. What can we still do?
items.answer: Use offline forms, training cards, local project data, local audio files, and prepare a package for later submission or physical transfer.
items.easyEnglish: Use offline forms, training cards, local project data, local audio files, and prepare a package for later submission or physical transfer. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Troubleshooting and offline-first training principles

items.question: What roles should a Recording Team have?
items.answer: Useful roles include Research lead, Script lead, Speaker care, Recorder operator, Backup person, Editor, Reviewer, Submitter, and Distribution/Share lead.
items.easyEnglish: Useful roles include Research lead, Script lead, Speaker care, Recorder operator, Backup person, Editor, Reviewer, Submitter, and Distribution/Share lead. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: Can one person have more than one role?
items.answer: Yes. Small teams may combine roles, but each role should still have a named owner so tasks do not disappear.
items.easyEnglish: Yes. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: How do we make a clean handoff?
items.answer: At the end of a stage, write what is complete, what is missing, who owns the next step, and what could block progress.
items.easyEnglish: At the end of a stage, write what is complete, what is missing, who owns the next step, and what could block progress. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: Who should care for speakers and helpers?
items.answer: Assign someone to explain the process, watch for fatigue or shame, help with breaks, and protect consent and dignity.
items.easyEnglish: Assign someone to explain the process, watch for fatigue or shame, help with breaks, and protect consent and dignity. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: Who should be responsible for backups?
items.answer: Name a backup person before recording begins. That person checks files, copies them safely, and records where the backups are stored.
items.easyEnglish: Name a backup person before recording begins. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: What does the reviewer do?
items.answer: The reviewer checks theological clarity, language accuracy, cultural clarity, permissions, metadata, and whether the program is ready for submission or sharing.
items.easyEnglish: The reviewer checks theological clarity, language accuracy, cultural clarity, permissions, metadata, and whether the program is ready for submission or sharing. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: How can experienced recordists help?
items.answer: Ask them for hidden knowledge, common mistakes, local tips, sample files, and realistic practice scenarios. Turn their advice into training cards.
items.easyEnglish: Ask them for hidden knowledge, common mistakes, local tips, sample files, and realistic practice scenarios. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: How can we reduce stress on one person?
items.answer: Divide tasks by strengths, use checklists, make handoffs visible, keep file naming consistent, and train more than one person in critical skills.
items.easyEnglish: Divide tasks by strengths, use checklists, make handoffs visible, keep file naming consistent, and train more than one person in critical skills. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: Who owns follow-up after sharing?
items.answer: Assign a Distribution/Share lead or local partner to collect feedback, testimonies, questions, and requests for more content.
items.easyEnglish: Assign a Distribution/Share lead or local partner to collect feedback, testimonies, questions, and requests for more content. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: How do we know the team is ready?
items.answer: The team can explain the workflow, complete forms without heavy correction, record clean audio, back up files, package correctly, and explain how the material will be used.
items.easyEnglish: The team can explain the workflow, complete forms without heavy correction, record clean audio, back up files, package correctly, and explain how the material will be used. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Team-based ministry, shared strengths, handoffs, readiness checks

items.question: Why not record only in the national language?
items.answer: The national language may reach some people, but the heart language often communicates trust, identity, emotion, and spiritual meaning more deeply. Research should show what listeners actually understand and prefer.
items.easyEnglish: The national language may reach some people, but the heart language often communicates trust, identity, emotion, and spiritual meaning more deeply. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: Should population size decide which language to record?
items.answer: Population matters, but it is not the only factor. Spiritual need, access, existing materials, partner requests, dialect barriers, and local opportunity also matter.
items.easyEnglish: Population matters, but it is not the only factor. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: How do we choose between two possible languages?
items.answer: Compare heart-language need, existing resources, partner readiness, access, urgency, speaker availability, and likely sharing path. Write the reason for the decision.
items.easyEnglish: Compare heart-language need, existing resources, partner readiness, access, urgency, speaker availability, and likely sharing path. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: How specific should the target listeners be?
items.answer: Be as specific as possible: children, women, elders, new believers, non-readers, church leaders, unreached villages, trauma survivors, or health message listeners may need different content.
items.easyEnglish: Be as specific as possible: children, women, elders, new believers, non-readers, church leaders, unreached villages, trauma survivors, or health message listeners may need different content. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: What changes for children’s ministry recordings?
items.answer: Use shorter sections, clear stories, natural voices, repetition, songs if appropriate, and safe sharing through trusted adults or churches.
items.easyEnglish: Use shorter sections, clear stories, natural voices, repetition, songs if appropriate, and safe sharing through trusted adults or churches. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: How should we plan a testimony?
items.answer: Keep it truthful, clear, culturally safe, and Christ-centered. Get consent, avoid unnecessary sensitive details, and protect identity if public sharing could cause risk.
items.easyEnglish: Keep it truthful, clear, culturally safe, and Christ-centered. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: How often should we take breaks?
items.answer: Take breaks before the speaker becomes tired or frustrated. Short breaks protect voice quality and help the speaker stay natural.
items.easyEnglish: Take breaks before the speaker becomes tired or frustrated. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: How do we record multiple speakers?
items.answer: Record one speaker at a time when possible, keep names and takes clear, and write who speaks in each file. If recording a group, test microphone placement carefully.
items.easyEnglish: Record one speaker at a time when possible, keep names and takes clear, and write who speaks in each file. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: What if a track is very long?
items.answer: Ask whether listeners can follow it. Consider dividing it into natural sections if the sharing method, audience, or format would benefit.
items.easyEnglish: Ask whether listeners can follow it. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: Who should do the final listen?
items.answer: Someone other than the editor should listen when possible. A fresh listener catches missing tracks, wrong order, bad edits, or unclear audio.
items.easyEnglish: Someone other than the editor should listen when possible. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: How should a physical submission be prepared?
items.answer: Use a labeled USB/SD/external drive, include a README, keep folder structure clear, and keep a backup before shipping or handing it off.
items.easyEnglish: Use a labeled USB/SD/external drive, include a README, keep folder structure clear, and keep a backup before shipping or handing it off. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: What should correction notes say?
items.answer: Write what changed, why it changed, who approved it, and which files replaced older versions. Keep it short and clear.
items.easyEnglish: Write what changed, why it changed, who approved it, and which files replaced older versions. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: Can we share by WhatsApp or Signal?
items.answer: Yes, if permissions and safety allow. Check file size, quality loss, language labels, and whether listeners can save or forward it appropriately.
items.easyEnglish: Yes, if permissions and safety allow. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: What should we check for radio sharing?
items.answer: Check permission, length, audio level, station requirements, language labels, local approval, and whether follow-up contact is announced.
items.easyEnglish: Check permission, length, audio level, station requirements, language labels, local approval, and whether follow-up contact is announced. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: What is a speaker box plan?
items.answer: Plan which device, who holds it, what files are loaded, battery charging, volume, group setting, and how feedback will be collected.
items.easyEnglish: Plan which device, who holds it, what files are loaded, battery charging, volume, group setting, and how feedback will be collected. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: Why should training lessons be short?
items.answer: Short lessons help adult learners practice quickly and remember better. Ten minutes of explanation plus hands-on practice often works better than long lectures.
items.easyEnglish: Short lessons help adult learners practice quickly and remember better. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: What should trainees practice first?
items.answer: Practice the real workflow: research a language, plan a short script, record a test, fill the log, name files, and explain sharing.
items.easyEnglish: Practice the real workflow: research a language, plan a short script, record a test, fill the log, name files, and explain sharing. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: What belongs in an offline kit?
items.answer: Include training videos, PDFs, forms, sample audio, practice files, checklists, installers or links, and a simple README for where to start.
items.easyEnglish: Include training videos, PDFs, forms, sample audio, practice files, checklists, installers or links, and a simple README for where to start. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.
items.sourceHint: Expanded practical FAQ

items.question: How should offline work sync later?
items.answer: Keep local project data organized, export a package, record what changed, and sync/upload when internet or a regional hub is available.
items.easyEnglish: Keep local project data organized, export a package, record what changed, and sync/upload when internet or a regional hub is available. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.

items.question: Tom gives too many related answers. What should I do?
items.answer: Use a stage filter like Record or Submit, and ask with fewer words: 'room tone', 'consent', 'file naming', or 'submit package'.
items.easyEnglish: Use a stage filter like Record or Submit, and ask with fewer words: 'room tone', 'consent', 'file naming', or 'submit package'. Use the checklist. Ask a trusted helper if you are not sure.

trainingCards.title: Confirm the Heart Language
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can explain which language or dialect should be recorded and why.
steps: List local names for the language.
Ask what people use at home.
Compare outside data with local interviews.
Mark each fact Confirmed, Likely, or Unknown.
Write one open question for follow-up.
commonMistakes: Assuming the national language is enough.
Copying web data without field verification.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Choose one community and complete a mini Language & Community Profile.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can explain which language or dialect should be recorded and why.

trainingCards.title: Find Cultural Bridges
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can identify local bridges that may help a script communicate clearly.
steps: Ask about local stories, proverbs, songs, fears, and daily life.
Write the bridge without changing biblical truth.
Ask a local believer if the bridge helps or confuses.
commonMistakes: Forcing a bridge that does not fit.
Changing Bible meaning to sound local.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Collect three possible bridges and mark one as best.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can identify local bridges that may help a script communicate clearly.

trainingCards.title: Adapt a Script Naturally
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can adapt a script for natural speech while protecting meaning.
steps: Ask how a respected local person would say it.
Ask for theological and local review.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Adapt one paragraph and write two reviewer questions.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can adapt a script for natural speech while protecting meaning.

trainingCards.title: Prepare Permissions and Consent
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can explain what permissions are needed before recording.
steps: List voices, songs, scripts, music, photos, and names.
Decide what will be shared locally or online.
Use the consent and rights forms.
Do not record public-use material without permission.
commonMistakes: Assuming verbal permission is enough for all uses.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Fill a sample consent form for a speaker.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can explain what permissions are needed before recording.

trainingCards.title: Record a Clean Test
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can set up, test, listen, adjust, and retest before a real session.
commonMistakes: Recording the whole script without testing.
Ignoring small noises that continue for the whole session.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Record two tests: one bad and one improved. Explain the difference.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can set up, test, listen, adjust, and retest before a real session.

trainingCards.title: Protect the Speaker
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can coach and correct a speaker without shame.
commonMistakes: Continuing when the speaker is tired.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can coach and correct a speaker without shame.

trainingCards.title: Build a Program Tracklist
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can organize tracks into a complete, understandable program.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Create a 5-track program from sample files.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can organize tracks into a complete, understandable program.

trainingCards.title: Prepare a Complete Package
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can make a package that another team can review without confusion.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Build a mock package and let another trainee check it.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can make a package that another team can review without confusion.

trainingCards.title: Plan Listener Access
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can choose sharing methods that fit the listeners.
commonMistakes: Using online-only sharing where internet is weak.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Design a sharing plan for one village and one church.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can choose sharing methods that fit the listeners.

trainingCards.title: Use Team Roles Wisely
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can assign workflow tasks to people, not just hope someone does them.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Assign roles for a three-person recording team.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can assign workflow tasks to people, not just hope someone does them.

trainingCards.title: Prepare a Rugged Offline Kit
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can work when internet fails.
steps: Save training cards and sample files.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Create a folder structure for an offline training kit.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can work when internet fails.

trainingCards.title: Diagnose Bad Audio Quickly
trainingCards.goal: Trainee can identify the top recording problems and first fixes.
steps: Check clipping, noise, echo, wind, hum, and quiet level.
Write the problem in the log.
commonMistakes: Trying to fix everything later in editing.
trainingCards.practiceTask: Listen to a bad sample and choose the first fix.
trainingCards.easyEnglish: Learn this one job: Trainee can identify the top recording problems and first fixes.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Distorted or clipped audio
troubleshootingFlows.trigger: Voice sounds harsh, crunchy, broken, or red peaks appear.
steps: Move microphone slightly away or off-axis.
Mark the bad take so it is not used.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when a clean retake is captured.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Too much background noise
troubleshootingFlows.trigger: Noise is clearly heard behind the speaker.
steps: Pause and identify the noise source.
Turn off fans, fridges, generators, phones, or noisy lights if possible.
Continue only if the noise is acceptable.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when the test sounds clear enough for ministry use.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Wind noise
troubleshootingFlows.trigger: Low rumble or blasts appear outdoors.
steps: Move indoors or behind a wind block.
Turn the mic away from direct wind.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when wind no longer distracts from the voice.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Nervous speaker
troubleshootingFlows.trigger: Speaker is tense, rushing, freezing, or apologizing often.
steps: Let a trusted helper sit nearby if appropriate.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when the speaker can continue calmly.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Dialect uncertainty
troubleshootingFlows.trigger: Team is not sure which dialect should be recorded.
steps: Mark the dialect as Unknown or Likely.
Record word lists or short stories from possible dialects.
Ask multiple trusted local listeners about understanding and acceptability.
Ask reviewer or partner before finalizing.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when the team has a confirmed or documented decision.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Upload failure
steps: Do not change the package randomly.
Check internet connection and file size.
Confirm the ZIP is not corrupted.
Use alternate approved transfer: USB, SD card, external drive, or local partner upload.
Write the handoff method in notes.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when the package is safely transferred or assigned for transfer.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Unsafe public sharing
troubleshootingFlows.trigger: Public sharing may endanger a speaker, believer, or community.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when a safer sharing method is chosen.

troubleshootingFlows.title: Tailender Tom cannot answer
troubleshootingFlows.trigger: Tom says he does not know or gives weak answers.
steps: Ask a shorter question with key words.
Add the approved answer to the knowledge base.
troubleshootingFlows.stopWhen: Stop when the question is answered or saved for review.
